He was arguably the most impressive winner all week at Ascot and he had the reopposing French Guineas winner Henri Matisse three and a half lengths back in second.

By Frankel and from a good family, he returned having been gelded after a 253-day layoff in June and scored in the manner of a progressive and capable type. Far From Dandy has met some trouble in-running on his last two starts and he is closely matched with the consistent Ja'marr on their Leopardstown clash in June.

selections.comment: Ralph Beckett holds a strong hand here with Sing Us A Song and Cape Breton. The former was left with far too much to do in a hot Royal Ascot handicap last time having blown the start but the form of his previous emphatic victory has been boosted so he should hold every chance if breaking on terms. The latter was untested when a winner from the front last time so is a big danger if allowed to dictate but this is a much stronger line up and he may may face competition up front. The pair may both be vulnerable to top weight OMNI MAN who did well to finish as close as he did at Ascot last time after meeting trouble turning into the straight. He's well treated on his previous maiden win and having proven himself versatile ground wise rates a solid option with Moore taking over.

selections.comment: A strong renewal where last year's first past the post Jabaara is hugely respected. She proved she retained her ability with a Listed win in the spring before racing too freely in the Queen Charlotte Stakes last time but should bounce back if settling. She will need to reverse form with the progressive Cloud Cover who boasts an excellent strike rate to go with her pair of recent Listed wins. If proving her effectiveness back on turf she should be thereabouts but the surface has to be a serious concern. The least exposed in the field TABITI may be the answer having run a huge race in the Sandringham on her reappearance. She was on the favourable part of the track but is entitled to come on for what was her first start since the autumn and will appreciate this drop back in trip. Moore takes over and she looks the one to be with.

She travelled best that day before being outstayed late over 6f by a classy rival who is now favourite for the Guineas next year. Back down over the minimum trip she can add to her previous Group victory at the expense of Sands Of Spain who has been progressing at a rate of knots and threw away the Super Sprint last time. On a line through the horses who defeated him that day he is closely matched with Ameeq and Dickensian here who both hold solid chances but are much shorter in the betting. Dual novice winner Military Code put his Ascot disappointment behind him when placed at Listed level last time and could also fight for a place behind the favourite.

selections.comment: Impossible to get away from FIELD OF GOLD who seeks a hat trick of wins at the top level after victories in the Irish Guineas and St James's Palace. He produced a big speed figure in the first of those wins and then a huge rating last time where he quickened clear of the field effortlessly a fair way out. He has 8lb in hand on his rivals on their UK form with the next bext Rosallion based on his victory in the same Ascot contest last year. He hasn't yet proven as good as he was prior to a lay off but has returned with placed efforts in the Lockinge and Queen Anne. He only lost on the bob to Docklands last time and is expected to reverse the form away from that rival's favoured venue. Strong staying French Guineas winner Henri Matisse may once again chase the selection home though he may get slightly closer this time with a clear run and a likely helpful strong pace set by his stablemate who has no chance on the figures.

MODEL YUKO was given a fine ride from the front when off the mark on the AW last time beating a couple of next time out winners. Her opening mark of 85 looks lenient based on that and further improvement can be expected over this longer trip based on her breeding. She can get the better of Music Piece who has seen the form of her Listed runner up effort here franked in the Sandringham at Royal Ascot and is forgiven her latest run on unsuitably quick ground. Wonder Star is another who disappointed last time but she looked potentially high class when landing a good novice on her penultimate start so is worth another chance on her handicap debut dropped in grade.

He is potentially thrown in on his 2yo Group form and open to improvement on just his second start over the trip. Great Acclaim was disappointing last time but is very interesting at a price based on his previous runner up effort behind Cracking Gold. The blinkers go on now and though all of his wins have come at 1m he should get a stiff test and has a good draw from which to attack. Veteran Billyjoh is also respected having placed in this last year off a higher mark. He has threatened in high end handicaps for a long time and his last run is worth marking up as he blew the start so he could get involved if turned out quickly.

selections.comment: BEACH PARTEE just about edges it on balance of form but the forecast fast ground is a potential spanner in the works as he struggled both times he's raced on a quick surface posting efforts some way below his other two runs on easier ground. It may be worth chancing the key factor wasn't the ground in those disappointing runs as he was patently outclasssed in the Listed Windsor Castle stakes at Royal Ascot on just his second start and then did too much at Nottingham next time tried over 6f for the first time. William Knight's colt gets the tentative vote. There are no such concerns regarding quick conditions with Dinamo and she could exploit any frailties in the selection having opened her account on her second start in nursery company on good to firm at Thirsk recently. Spirit Star and Brightling have claims but Baybe Driver is feared more if able to show his latest run wrong when failing to stay 6f at Chester having raced free. Dropped back to 5f he can get back on track and the fast ground shouldn't hinder his propsects like it might for a number of his rivals

selections.comment: Versailles Prince is interesting on handicap bow off a workable looking mark upped to 1m2f for the first time having looked in need of a greater stamina test than the mile he's tackled all three career runs. He can take a step forward and lay down a determined challenge. However, GLORYOUS took a big step forward with a commanding win last at Sandown over 1m2f on good ground. He had previously gone very close on fast ground and should be kept onside for now with the potential for a bit more yet. Appleblossomwhite has to show she's recovered form an unseating on her hurdles debut last time and a below par effort prior to that on the Flat over a mile. However, she hit a career high when fifth of 11 first time over 1m2f in late May and if coping with faster conditions could play a significant role. She's preferred to Hibernate who takes a step up the class ladder having scraped home last time in a class 6 handicap and Verasion, who has form claims but has serious stamina concerns

selections.comment: Willie Mullins holds a strong hand here with Gorvitho and HIPOP DE LOIRE. The former is forgiven his latest run which he needed and better judged on his debut effort where placed behind a useful rival who went on to place in the Martin Pipe. He may however find the ground on the fast side and his stablemate looks the solid option here. The selection was only narrowly denied at this meeting last year on his hurdle debut and proved he retained his ability with a solid Listed flat run this term. Given he was successful at this level on the flat when trained in Germany it is likely he has much more to offer in this discipline for his top stable. The greatest threat may come from the useful experienced dual purpose performer Zanndabad who went close in the Chester Cup last year and probably sets the standard in this sphere on his UK novice events on good ground which is key to him.

He's entitled to come on for that returning run and is potentially thrown in on his form prior to a lay off so should be a big threat here. If getting a run veteran The Little Yank would also be respected as he has been in excellent form over hurdles and fences of late off a much reduced mark.

selections.comment: An open race as ever but the unexposed DOWN MEMORY LANE gets the narrow verdict. He brings in some strong Grade 1 novice form from last season despite being unsuited by the testing ground those days and is a likely improver now handicapping off a lenient mark up in trip on favourable good ground. Ashdale Bob is another possible improver after running well for a long way on his recent handicap debut back from a break. He should come on for that and is well treated on both his best hurdle form and his Graded chase win here last autumn. Joseph O'Brien holds a strong hand with dual purpose performers Nurburgring and Common Practice. The former landed the feature hurdle here last year before placing at Cheltenham and Royal Ascot this year in different disciplines. He's open to further improvement over fences if brushing up on his jumping. His stablemate has been in good form in both codes this year including taking a Graded contest in the spring and could find a bit more in the first time blinkers. Consistent staying chaser Amirite also has blinkers added and completes the list of dangers following a Midlands National victory last time.

selections.comment: Joseph O'Brien holds a strong hand here with Light Up The Dark and Shoda. The former is a dual bumper winner who was off the mark in this sphere last time and likely has more to offer now handicapping over further so holds strong claims. However his stablemate is the first string on jockey bookings and has plenty of mileage in her make based on her spring Graded hurdle form. She was poorly placed to challenge at a sharp track on her flat return but finished full of running and looks a likely improver now upped to 2m for the first time. Both of those hold solid claims but could be vulnerable to another dual purpose performer in the shape of FEUD who was a hurdles winner at this meeting last year beating a couple of next time out winners. He was unsuited by the steady pace and sharp track on his flat return but finished off his race well suggesting that this longer trip would be of benefit. If the first time cheekpieces can help him lay up early he should be thereabouts at the finish off what looks a generous mark based on his old UK flat form.
